chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-A'la, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, "Is obedience to the awsiya' obligatory?" He said, "Yes."
They are those about whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those vested with authority from among you."
And they are those about whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "Your wali is only Allah and His Messenger and those who believe, those who establish salat and give zakat while they are bowing."

key_terms.أُولِي الْأَمْرِ: those vested with authority whose obedience is commanded
key_terms.الْأَوْصِيَاءُ: the designated successors entrusted with divine authority after the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.رَاكِعُونَ: while in the state of bowing
key_terms.طَاعَتُهُمْ: obedience to them as a binding religious duty
key_terms.يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلَاةَ: they establish salat consistently and properly

ai.seo_question: Does the Quran command obedience to the Imams and the awsiya'?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms that obedience to the awsiya' is divinely mandated. Imam Abu Abdillah عليه السلام identifies them as the referents of the Quranic verses concerning ulu al-amr and wilayah, linking the authority of the Imams to explicit Quranic designation.
